title: Who Has Access to Claude? Bring AI Identity and Access Context Into Surface Command
content_md: Approving an AI service is only the starting point. As employees adopt Claude and their responsibilities change, security teams need to know who has access, which users hold administrative privileges, and whether those roles and group memberships still reflect the work they do. IBM’s 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that, among studied organizations reporting an AI-related breach, 97% lacked proper AI access controls. The finding highlights a broader challenge: AI adoption needs security practices that extend beyond the initial approval, supported by information teams can use to review access with administrators and service owners. Rapid7 Surface Command now integrates with Claude’s Compliance API, bringing supported organization, user, role, group, and settings information into the same platform teams use to understand other assets and identities. The integration helps security teams make enterprise Claude access part of their existing review practices. Bring enterprise AI access into your security view An account list tells security teams who is present, while roles and group memberships help explain how access is organized and where further review may be needed. Surface Command’s integration with Claude’s Compliance API brings together: Organizations and users: Visibility into the Claude organization and its associated user accounts. Roles and groups: Context to understand users’ assigned roles and group memberships. Organizational settings: Available configuration
exclude_reason: Rapid7 product promotion for Claude access governance, not a security event.
